## Employee
- Name: Sagnibha Roy (no id)
- Role: Maintenance Planner, Maintenance
- Plant / unit: Raiganj  / Unit 100

## Equipment history in the knowledge graph
- none found for this profile; interview from the profile alone and ask them to name their key equipment

topics.title: Role Transition Challenges and Unwritten Workflows
topics.rationale: Understanding the undocumented aspects of the planner role to ensure smooth transition.
seed_questions: What daily tasks consume the most time but are not captured in the official procedures?
How do you prioritize emergency work orders when they conflict with planned maintenance?
Which stakeholders outside the formal chain do you rely on to get things done?

topics.title: Unfinished Maintenance Improvement Projects
topics.rationale: Capturing the state and lessons from any improvement initiatives to avoid rework or loss of momentum.
seed_questions: Can you list the maintenance improvement projects you started or were part of?
Which ones are only half-finished and what are the key blockers?
What would be the first steps to revive them?

topics.title: Critical Equipment Inventory and Undocumented Histories
topics.rationale: Populate the knowledge graph with key assets not yet documented, along with their known failure patterns.
seed_questions: What are the top 5 most critical pieces of rotating equipment in Unit 100 that you worry about?
For each, what are the recurring failure modes that are not recorded in the CMMS?
Are there any workarounds or temporary fixes currently in place?

topics.title: Non-Stocked Spare Parts and Vendor Lead Times
topics.rationale: To capture unofficial knowledge about spares that are required but not on the shelf, and which vendors can expedite.
seed_questions: Which spare parts for Unit 100 equipment do you keep hidden away or know have to be ordered far in advance?
Are there alternative vendors you use when official lead times are too long?
What’s the one spare part that would cause a prolonged outage if it failed?

topics.title: Undocumented Equipment Idiosyncrasies and Workarounds
topics.rationale: Ensure that unwritten operational adjustments and bypasses known only to the planner are not lost.
seed_questions: Are there any equipment interlocks that you regularly bypass or adjust unofficially to keep running?
What are the telltale signs that a machine is about to fail that operators ignore?
What is the most common ‘field fix’ that you’ve never written down because it’s too complex?

topics.title: Gap Between Planned Maintenance Procedures and Reality
topics.rationale: Learn where formal procedures are unsafe, inefficient, or outdated and what the actual practice is.
seed_questions: Which standard operating procedures in the maintenance plan do you think are dangerously wrong?
How do you actually perform lockout/tagout in Unit 100 versus what the procedure says?
Are there any tasks where you routinely skip or shorten the procedure to meet production targets?

topics.title: Shutdown and Turnaround Planning Tricks
topics.rationale: Acquire the heuristic knowledge used for scheduling plant turnarounds that is not in the manuals.
seed_questions: When planning a major shutdown, how do you estimate the true duration versus the official schedule?
What activities always get squeezed for time but are critical?
Who do you call first when a shutdown overruns?

topics.title: Vendor and Contractor Relational Knowledge
topics.rationale: Personal relationships and unofficial service expectations are crucial for expediting repairs.
seed_questions: Which vendor technicians do you trust implicitly and have a direct line to?
Which contractor companies always overpromise and underdeliver?
What’s the understanding you have with the local machine shop that isn’t in any contract?

topics.title: Operations-Maintenance Interface Friction
topics.rationale: Understanding the informal negotiation and communication patterns used to get equipment released for maintenance.
seed_questions: How do you convince operations to hand over a piece of equipment when they are behind on production targets?
What are the unwritten rules about which operators are easiest to work with?
Are there any conflicts you routinely manage between maintenance staff and operations that are never escalated?

topics.title: CMMS and Digital System Transition State
topics.rationale: If any computer system changes are in progress or planned, we need to know the current state, workarounds, and data gaps.
seed_questions: What is the status of the Computerized Maintenance Management System upgrade or migration?
Are there any data entry shortcuts or workarounds you use that your successor will need?
Which reports do you generate manually because the system can’t do it?

topics.title: Maintenance Budget and Resource Allocation Tricks
topics.rationale: Unofficial methods for stretching the maintenance budget or prioritizing work with limited resources.
seed_questions: How do you actually manage your maintenance budget given that official figures never match reality?
Which cost centers do you hide expenses in?
What is the one resource (e.g., speciality crew, tool) that is always oversubscribed and how do you schedule around that?

topics.title: Open Risks and Successor Advice
topics.rationale: Handover of ongoing issues and top risks, plus any advice for the incoming planner.
seed_questions: What are the top three risks that could cause a plant slowdown or safety incident in the next 3 months?
If you could only give your successor one piece of advice to be successful in this role, what would it be?
What is the biggest mistake a new planner could make in Unit 100?

topics.title: Past Equipment Failures and Lessons Learned Not in the System
topics.rationale: Capturing significant failures and the root causes that were not formally documented.
seed_questions: Tell me about a major equipment failure that you dealt with where the official report didn’t capture the full truth.
What really happened and what was the real root cause?
How did you prevent it from happening again, unofficially?

topics.title: Preventive Maintenance Optimization: Hidden Insights
topics.rationale: Capture what he has learned about which PM tasks are waste, which are too infrequent, and how to adjust them.
seed_questions: Which PM tasks do you think are a complete waste of time?
Which equipment should have MORE frequent checks but don’t because of resource limits?
How do you decide when to move from time-based to condition-based maintenance?

topics.title: Personal Knowledge Management and Reference Tricks
topics.rationale: How does the planner keep track of details, such as notes, contacts, drawings, that aren’t in the official system.
seed_questions: Do you have a personal notebook, spreadsheet, or mental model you use?
Where do you keep critical dimensions, setpoints, or interlock details that aren’t in the CMMS?
Who should your successor call when they can’t find a drawing?
